items.title: The Gunpowder Age: China, Military Innovation, and the Rise of the West in World History
items.note: Global synthesis that places the arrival of gunpowder in Europe in the context of Mongol-era contact.

items.title: The Gunpowder Age: China, Military Innovation, and the Rise of the West in World History (review forum), with Culture and Context: Reflections on The Gunpowder Age
items.who: P. Hoffman, I. Inkster, S. Morillo, D. Parrott, K. Pomeranz; reply by T. Andrade
items.note: Historians of European warfare and technology assess Andrade's account of early gunpowder and its westward spread; Andrade's reply follows (doi:10.1017/jch.2018.18).

items.title: An Earth-shattering kaboom!: The Mongols and the use and transmission of gunpowder
items.venue: Central Eurasian Studies Society conference, Pittsburgh
items.note: Revisits whether the Mongols used gunpowder outside East Asia, how Roger Bacon got his recipe, and why early European guns resemble Yuan ones.

items.title: Confucian Statecraft and the Production of Saltpeter and Sulfur in Song Dynasty China
items.venue: Science and Confucian Statecraft in East Asia (Brill)
items.note: Examines how the Song state organised saltpetre and sulphur supply, the production base that any account of westward transmission starts from.

items.title: Revisiting the Dazu "Bombard" and the World's Earliest Representation of a Gun
items.note: Argues that the evidence for reading the Dazu cave sculpture as a c. 1128 gun is inadequate, unsettling an early anchor in the Chinese chronology.

items.title: Four Misunderstood Gunpowder Recipes of the Fourteenth Century
items.note: Re-reads four fourteenth-century European gunpowder recipes, arguing that earlier interpretations of their proportions and purpose were mistaken.

items.title: The Earliest Middle English Recipes for Gunpowder
items.note: Presents the earliest gunpowder recipes in Middle English, adding vernacular witnesses to the early European recipe record.

items.title: Gunpowder Technology in the Fifteenth Century: A Study, Edition and Translation of the Firework Book
items.note: First full edition and translation of a Feuerwerkbuch manuscript, clarifying the later European recipe tradition against which earlier sources must be read.

items.title: Joseph Needham and the Theory of the Origin of Gunpowder in Tang Dynasty
items.venue: Studies in the History of Natural Sciences
items.note: Reassesses how Needham built the case for a Tang-dynasty alchemical origin of gunpowder, the starting point of the transmission chronology.
